{
  "project_id": "P-UK-FreeBreakfastClubs",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Delay in passage of the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill could postpone the mandatory duty, leaving schools without a legal requirement to run free breakfast clubs.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Engage early with legislative drafters, develop interim voluntary guidance for schools, and prepare a contingency rollout plan.",
      "evidence": "The Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill will place a duty on state-funded schools to offer a breakfast club."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Future years’ funding may not be secured, threatening programme continuity after year 1.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Prepare a robust multi‑year business case, secure provisional budget commitments, and set aside a contingency reserve.",
      "evidence": "Funding for future years will be agreed separately through business cases."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "The internal CRM system may not be ready by the November 2025 MVP deadline, hindering school onboarding and support.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Allocate a dedicated development team, adopt agile milestones, and retain a manual onboarding fallback process.",
      "evidence": "Develop a customer relationship management system internally, working towards a minimum‑viable product from November 2025."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "The call‑centre pilot for data collection could fail to capture accurate attendance data, affecting funding calculations and monitoring.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Pilot with clear KPIs, conduct early user testing, and retain school self‑reporting as a backup data source.",
      "evidence": "Start commercial processes to begin a call‑centre pilot to support data collection."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Cohort 1 schools may miss the April 2026 start date, compressing implementation timelines.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Set weekly progress checkpoints, provide early guidance packs, and allocate rapid‑response support for delayed schools.",
      "evidence": "Cohort 1 will begin delivery in April 2026."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "A gap between the NSBP ending in July 2026 and FBC start in September 2026 could leave pupils without breakfast provision.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Arrange interim bridging provision, communicate transition timelines early, and align procurement to ensure continuity.",
      "evidence": "NSBP will end in July 2026... invited to join the FBC programme, starting in September 2026."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Complexity of the funding model may cause confusion among schools, reducing uptake.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Produce clear guidance, run webinars, and offer a dedicated help‑desk to answer funding queries.",
      "evidence": "Variation by disadvantage levels was deemed complicated; simplified model intended to be easier to understand."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Insufficient staffing for supervised childcare and food preparation could compromise club quality, especially in high‑disadvantage schools.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Provide recruitment incentives, leverage local‑authority staffing support, and allow flexible staffing ratios where appropriate.",
      "evidence": "Staffing levels are estimated and rounded... typical staffing patterns for mainstream, SEND and specialist settings."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Food supply chain disruptions may prevent schools from meeting required food standards.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Qualify multiple approved suppliers, maintain buffer stock, and monitor market conditions continuously.",
      "evidence": "Food provided must be in line with school food standards."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Labour‑market inflation could outpace area cost adjustments, leading to under‑funded schools.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Review area adjustments annually and embed an inflation buffer within the funding formula.",
      "evidence": "Apply an area cost adjustment to the funding to account for variations in the labour market."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Persistently high pupil absence post‑pandemic may lower club take‑up, weakening the projected benefit‑cost ratio.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Promote health‑safety measures, offer flexible attendance options, and monitor attendance trends to adjust outreach.",
      "evidence": "School absence significantly increased following the pandemic... still not returned to pre‑pandemic levels."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Advisers procured via the education and children’s social care framework may under‑perform, affecting school support.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Include strict performance clauses, conduct regular monitoring, and retain internal backup advisers.",
      "evidence": "Procurement process to increase the number of advisers supporting schools through the educational and children's social care framework."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "The independent evaluation may not deliver timely insights, limiting programme adjustments.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Set clear interim reporting milestones, appoint an evaluation steering committee, and ensure rapid dissemination of findings.",
      "evidence": "Evaluation will be independently commissioned and run from 2026 to 2028, with interim and final reporting."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "A change in government priorities could reduce political support and resources for the programme.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Embed the duty in legislation, build cross‑party advocacy, and showcase early success metrics.",
      "evidence": "The government has committed to create a new mandatory free breakfast club duty for all state‑funded schools."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Data‑privacy concerns around the CRM and call‑centre could lead to compliance breaches.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Conduct a Data Protection Impact Assessment, enforce GDPR‑compliant safeguards, and provide staff training.",
      "evidence": "Develop a customer relationship management system... schools engage with the department for 'first line' support."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R16",
      "description": "Funding rates for special schools may be insufficient given higher per‑child costs, creating inequitable provision.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Monitor special‑school cost data and adjust the per‑child rate if disparities emerge.",
      "evidence": "At special schools, the funding rate is: £1,000 start‑up grant, daily amount of £18.95, £3.23 for every child."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R17",
      "description": "Governance processes may not flag emerging issues promptly, delaying corrective action.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Enforce monthly project‑board reviews, define clear escalation paths, and assign dedicated risk owners.",
      "evidence": "Risks and issues are reviewed regularly, with challenges escalated as appropriate to the SRO and project directors through the monthly project board."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R18",
      "description": "Area cost adjustments could over‑fund low‑cost regions, wasting taxpayer money.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 2,
      "mitigation": "Periodically recalibrate adjustments against actual cost data and adjust allocations accordingly.",
      "evidence": "Apply an area cost adjustment to the funding to account for variations in the labour market."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R19",
      "description": "Schools not meeting the 40% FSM threshold for Cohort 1 may feel excluded, harming stakeholder relations.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 2,
      "mitigation": "Communicate transparent eligibility criteria and offer alternative support mechanisms for other schools.",
      "evidence": "Cohort 1... schools with 40% or more FSM 'Ever 6' pupils will be eligible to apply for a place."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R20",
      "description": "If attainment benefits are lower than forecast, the benefit‑cost ratio could fall below 1, questioning value for money.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Track early attainment outcomes, adjust programme scale, and implement cost‑efficiency measures as needed.",
      "evidence": "Sensitivity analysis halving attainment benefits still returns a positive BCR of 1.19."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Delay in passage of the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill could postpone the mandatory duty, leaving schools without a legal requirement to run free breakfast clubs.
risks.mitigation: Engage early with legislative drafters, develop interim voluntary guidance for schools, and prepare a contingency rollout plan.
risks.evidence: The Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill will place a duty on state-funded schools to offer a breakfast club.

risks.description: Future years’ funding may not be secured, threatening programme continuity after year 1.
risks.mitigation: Prepare a robust multi‑year business case, secure provisional budget commitments, and set aside a contingency reserve.
risks.evidence: Funding for future years will be agreed separately through business cases.

risks.description: The internal CRM system may not be ready by the November 2025 MVP deadline, hindering school onboarding and support.
risks.mitigation: Allocate a dedicated development team, adopt agile milestones, and retain a manual onboarding fallback process.
risks.evidence: Develop a customer relationship management system internally, working towards a minimum‑viable product from November 2025.

risks.description: The call‑centre pilot for data collection could fail to capture accurate attendance data, affecting funding calculations and monitoring.
risks.mitigation: Pilot with clear KPIs, conduct early user testing, and retain school self‑reporting as a backup data source.
risks.evidence: Start commercial processes to begin a call‑centre pilot to support data collection.

risks.description: Cohort 1 schools may miss the April 2026 start date, compressing implementation timelines.
risks.mitigation: Set weekly progress checkpoints, provide early guidance packs, and allocate rapid‑response support for delayed schools.
risks.evidence: Cohort 1 will begin delivery in April 2026.

risks.description: A gap between the NSBP ending in July 2026 and FBC start in September 2026 could leave pupils without breakfast provision.
risks.mitigation: Arrange interim bridging provision, communicate transition timelines early, and align procurement to ensure continuity.
risks.evidence: NSBP will end in July 2026... invited to join the FBC programme, starting in September 2026.

risks.description: Complexity of the funding model may cause confusion among schools, reducing uptake.
risks.mitigation: Produce clear guidance, run webinars, and offer a dedicated help‑desk to answer funding queries.
risks.evidence: Variation by disadvantage levels was deemed complicated; simplified model intended to be easier to understand.

risks.description: Insufficient staffing for supervised childcare and food preparation could compromise club quality, especially in high‑disadvantage schools.
risks.mitigation: Provide recruitment incentives, leverage local‑authority staffing support, and allow flexible staffing ratios where appropriate.
risks.evidence: Staffing levels are estimated and rounded... typical staffing patterns for mainstream, SEND and specialist settings.

risks.description: Food supply chain disruptions may prevent schools from meeting required food standards.
risks.mitigation: Qualify multiple approved suppliers, maintain buffer stock, and monitor market conditions continuously.
risks.evidence: Food provided must be in line with school food standards.

risks.description: Labour‑market inflation could outpace area cost adjustments, leading to under‑funded schools.
risks.mitigation: Review area adjustments annually and embed an inflation buffer within the funding formula.
risks.evidence: Apply an area cost adjustment to the funding to account for variations in the labour market.

risks.description: Persistently high pupil absence post‑pandemic may lower club take‑up, weakening the projected benefit‑cost ratio.
risks.mitigation: Promote health‑safety measures, offer flexible attendance options, and monitor attendance trends to adjust outreach.
risks.evidence: School absence significantly increased following the pandemic... still not returned to pre‑pandemic levels.

risks.description: Advisers procured via the education and children’s social care framework may under‑perform, affecting school support.
risks.mitigation: Include strict performance clauses, conduct regular monitoring, and retain internal backup advisers.
risks.evidence: Procurement process to increase the number of advisers supporting schools through the educational and children's social care framework.

risks.description: The independent evaluation may not deliver timely insights, limiting programme adjustments.
risks.mitigation: Set clear interim reporting milestones, appoint an evaluation steering committee, and ensure rapid dissemination of findings.
risks.evidence: Evaluation will be independently commissioned and run from 2026 to 2028, with interim and final reporting.

risks.description: A change in government priorities could reduce political support and resources for the programme.
risks.mitigation: Embed the duty in legislation, build cross‑party advocacy, and showcase early success metrics.
risks.evidence: The government has committed to create a new mandatory free breakfast club duty for all state‑funded schools.

risks.description: Data‑privacy concerns around the CRM and call‑centre could lead to compliance breaches.
risks.mitigation: Conduct a Data Protection Impact Assessment, enforce GDPR‑compliant safeguards, and provide staff training.
risks.evidence: Develop a customer relationship management system... schools engage with the department for 'first line' support.

risks.description: Funding rates for special schools may be insufficient given higher per‑child costs, creating inequitable provision.
risks.mitigation: Monitor special‑school cost data and adjust the per‑child rate if disparities emerge.
risks.evidence: At special schools, the funding rate is: £1,000 start‑up grant, daily amount of £18.95, £3.23 for every child.

risks.description: Governance processes may not flag emerging issues promptly, delaying corrective action.
risks.mitigation: Enforce monthly project‑board reviews, define clear escalation paths, and assign dedicated risk owners.
risks.evidence: Risks and issues are reviewed regularly, with challenges escalated as appropriate to the SRO and project directors through the monthly project board.

risks.description: Area cost adjustments could over‑fund low‑cost regions, wasting taxpayer money.
risks.mitigation: Periodically recalibrate adjustments against actual cost data and adjust allocations accordingly.
risks.evidence: Apply an area cost adjustment to the funding to account for variations in the labour market.

risks.description: Schools not meeting the 40% FSM threshold for Cohort 1 may feel excluded, harming stakeholder relations.
risks.mitigation: Communicate transparent eligibility criteria and offer alternative support mechanisms for other schools.
risks.evidence: Cohort 1... schools with 40% or more FSM 'Ever 6' pupils will be eligible to apply for a place.

risks.description: If attainment benefits are lower than forecast, the benefit‑cost ratio could fall below 1, questioning value for money.
risks.mitigation: Track early attainment outcomes, adjust programme scale, and implement cost‑efficiency measures as needed.
risks.evidence: Sensitivity analysis halving attainment benefits still returns a positive BCR of 1.19.
